title: Service Bus, Event Grid and Event Hubs: queue, event and stream

videos.script: Lesson 15 started a function from a storage queue. This lesson is about the three Azure services that carry work and news between systems, and why there are three. {{three}} Service Bus holds a message until one consumer settles it. Event Grid pushes a notice to every subscriber that asked for it. Event Hubs keeps a stream in order, and every reader keeps its own place in it. {{queue}} You start with a Service Bus queue, in Microsoft's emulator, on your laptop. Receiving a message locks it. It does not remove it. You will abandon one three times and find it in the dead-letter queue. {{topic}} Then a topic that gives billing every order and shipping only the ones with something to ship. Then sessions, which keep one order's steps in order. {{grid}} Event Grid has no emulator, so you read it, and compile its subscription. {{hubs}} Then Event Hubs: two partitions, two consumer groups, two positions in the same log. Last, the promise all three make. At least once. You will watch a second delivery happen, and see what makes it harmless. {{dupes}}
